questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The location and the culture based on what I have heard from other students.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I received a lot of e-mails prior to my arrival at my study destination. They were filled with all the information I needed upon arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: My study destination had a Student Mobility office, where we could send e-mails to or meet in person if we had any problems. There was also IT-support.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my accommodation through Airbnb, but we got a contract outside of Airbnb. That worked really well.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I found my accommodation through Airbnb, but we got a contract outside of Airbnb. That worked really well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was fine. We just needed to send an application with the most important information and a photo of ourselves.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Again, the Student Mobility Office was helpful if we needed any help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Because you need to attend all the classes, we had to make sure we didn't have any overlapping courses. That made me drop some courses I would have liked to attend. Other than that, no problems.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to check for overlapping courses and try to organize your schedule in such a way, that you don't have too big breaks during the day, really late classes etc.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Because all the courses had an empirical approach, the level of the courses seemed lower than UCPH. There were no theoretical perspectives.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Really different educational approach. There were no theories, all the courses had an empirical approach. The assessment was based on class presentations, tests and oral exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: African Politics And Society; Asian Culture and Politics; Political Thought In The Mena; Culture, Policy And Society; Heritage, Tourism and Economic Development Policies; The EU External Action

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Most courses were business orientated courses, so look through the course catalogue for the few good ones for Political Science.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Really high gas bills

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Gas bills were more expensive than expected. Museum tickets were less expensive than expected, as you can get really good discounts if you are under 25.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival, the Erasmus Student Network have organized a whole Welcome Week for all new Erasmus students. ESN also plan many social activities throughout the semester, which you can go to if you want.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Get a recommendation list from a former exchange student with all the good spots :)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: In Rome, when the weather gets really hot, go to the lake or the beach to cool down! It is only about an hour of transportation and it is really worth it! Also go to other cities in Italy, there are so many amazing places

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy! Everyone are really friendly. The only thing that can be hard to adjust to, is that the busses do not come on time....

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If you want to meet a lot of local students, then go to the ESN activities

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Hmmmm, I don't know :)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Italian food and of course the amazing big gestures, facial expressions and mannerism

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Live close to the university, it makes the everyday life more easy
Try to take one day per week to do all kinds of cultural stuff and see the city 
Eat a lot of pasta!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Finding accommodation through Airbnb worked well for me

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Really amazing new friends <33

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not being able to bike everywhere, but having to either walk or wait for busses that does not show

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
